text.p: Here are the leading stories reported by Lithuania's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas supported the move by the Centre Union party to amend the constitution to make it easier for Lithuanians residing abroad to be a candidate in presidential elections.
- High ranking officials of the Kaunas tax inspection suspected defrauding the budget of one million litas may go to court.

- A shareholder meeting of 84 percent state-run Klaipeda Stevedoring decided to double its share capital from reserves by 128.99 million litas. The new shares will be acquired proportionally by present owners.
- Lithuanian Gas had a 15.975 million litas loss in 1996. Director general of the company Kestutis Shumacheris said the 69.72 million litas debt to Lentrasgaz was acknowledged as state debt.
- Utenos Beverages light beer was awarded a bronze medal by a U.S. magazine.
- The government is expected to decide on higher electric energy tariffs at the next cabinet meeting. The price for one kilowatt may rise to 22 cents from 20 cents.

- The increase of prices in April reduced the popularity of the government by nine percent, an opinion poll by Baltic Surveys showed. Trust in the Bank of Lithuania and police rose four percent to 34 and 27 percent.
- The Christian Democrats oppose the construction of an ammonia production workshop at the huge Achema fertiliser plant.

- A Baltic Surveys poll showed a fall in popularity among leading politicians. The list was led by Brazauskas, U.S. enviroment expert Valdas Admakus and former deputy prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas. Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius was ranked seventh.
- Vagnorius told the newspaper that employees of state-run companies slated for privatisation will benefit most.
- The inflation in Lithuania in March was the lowest among the Baltic countries.
